body:
DESIGN, N-26 / B-125 (helper-n26). No code yet. Full text: docs/tasks/P2-songs-as-references.md, section "N-26" under P2-04 (docs PR).

CAUSE, PROVED (real functions on the live clone's code; JSON constructed from a recorded entry, title and channel strings real):
- The stored rows (KEXP / ARTE Concert / Crunchyroll, song = the whole video title) come from the YouTube Music reader: _ytmusic_tracks takes artists[0] (the uploader, for an upload) for EVERY videoType and never reads the title. With the three real titles+channels and videoType UGC (or none) it returns exactly the stored rows.
- The yt-dlp reader (fallback) is wrong differently: "Tinariwen - Full Performance (Live on KEXP)" / KEXP gives artist "Full Performance (Live on KEXP)", song "Tinariwen" (_is_channel is a substring test: "kexp" is inside the right side, so the sides swap). ARTE (en dash is no separator) and Crunchyroll (no " - ") give artist = channel. _fold is ASCII-only: a non-Latin name folds to "" (B-37 trap).
- The matcher is not at fault (it reads a CANDIDATE's channel as evidence; a Candidate never becomes a ref's artist). File import: the file's own artist column.
- TRAP: C:/dev/venv-encore-server has encore_server installed from the OLD archive clone encore\ . A script by path (or python -I) imports it; python -m pytest / python -c from the live clone's server/encore_server imports the right copy: print encore_server.__file__. Baseline test_import_readers + test_imports: 74 passed.

RULE: the channel is the uploader, and the uploader is evidence, not the artist. ONE function read_upload(title, uploader, kind, declared) -> (artist, song, basis); both readers (later the file import and P2-12) call it.
- ATV / OFFICIAL_SOURCE_MUSIC / OMV, or no videoType on an unavailable-or-with-album entry: trust YouTube Music's artists, basis declared (146+1+2 recorded entries: unchanged; an invariance test over all 149+10 blocks slice 1).
- UGC, ANY unknown videoType, yt-dlp listing: read the title. Any dash (hyphen/en/em, spaces, outside brackets) = Artist - Song; the channel flips it to Song - Artist only when it is a WHOLE NAME (Unicode-folded; Official/VEVO/Topic removed; or one name of a credit list) of the right side, never a substring. Brackets never decide. basis title, EXCEPT when the artist is reached only because the whole right side equals the uploader and names nobody else ("... - ARTE Concert"): then basis channel (a broadcaster and a performer look the same there), so slices 2+3 protect it; cost: a performer's own "Song - Artist" upload is weak too, absorbed by "a name with one declared/title song is an artist".
- No dash: the uploader, basis channel = the one named stop-gap. Unknowable from YouTube alone: U1 a personal upload account whose title names nobody (looks the same as the band's own channel), U2 order of sides when neither is the channel, U3 an upload that is not a song, U4 performer only in the description. Removal trigger: catalogue identification from the title (P2-12 / N-14); proposed task N-26b.

SLICES, each merges alone: 1 (M) read_upload + videoType gate + whole-name Unicode test + all dashes + fixtures (step 0: record real get_playlist answers, <=10 look-ups spaced, extend tools/record_ytm_fixtures.py, incl. an OMV from a LABEL channel). 2 (S) song_ref.artist_basis + uploader (importer-only, never from a client's JSON); artist_finder skips names whose songs are ALL channel; _enrich never rewrites an artist. 3 (S-M) no artist page for a channel: PROOF first on the real music server in CI, then the keeper's tags. 4 (S) context shapes (live-session credit, "Opening | Song by Artist") only with a negative corpus. 5 (M-L) repair of stored rows, trigger-gated.
After slice 1 alone: Tinariwen is filed under Tinariwen; ARTE Concert and Crunchyroll stay under their channels until slice 4.
